title: The partial-success shape of a selection and its summary message are not typed
source: Legacy story RWB E2 012 v2 sections 4, 13 and 16 (BulkTransferRunner, MSG-P3-035); FSD P3 Case and workflow v4 A2.40.4.3 AC-EXC-P3-040-04; TSD P3 Case and workflow v3 API-P3-006
section: 4 Flow; 7 Acceptance criteria (AC3, AC11); 12 Contract (12.1); 13 Solution plan
description: The legacy screen sends one request per selected case and renders one row per case plus a summary, and the legacy AC11 fixes the outcome as 8 of 10 moved with the two held cases showing MSG-P3-005 and the summary showing MSG-P3-035. No source types the element a row is rendered from, its order, its required fields, or how the summary counts are carried: the transfer operation is declared per case and has no set-level request or response, and the summary is a message text with two placeholders and no schema.
evidence: Legacy section 4 step 8 'for a bulk move, one result per case and the summary'; section 13 'BulkTransferRunner | Sends one request per selected case in sequence and collects the results'; FSD AC-EXC-P3-040-04 'eight cases move And the two held cases show MSG-P3-005 And the summary shows MSG-P3-035 with 8 of 10'; TSD API-P3-006 Request TransferRequest Response Assignment, with no set-level operation anywhere in the P3 API inventory; MSG-P3-035 '{done} of {total} cases were moved. The others show the reason on their row.' has no field table.
owner_role: Solution architect, P3; tech lead of rwb-case
proposed: Fix one selection element in the rwb-case contract: an ordered array with caseId, the assignment or the messageId of the refusal, and the done and total counts; state that the order is the caller's order and that the summary is derived from the array and never from a second call.

title: The at-cap and legal-hold pre-check answers have no typed shape
source: Legacy story RWB E2 012 v2 sections 4, 12 and 14; FSD P3 Case and workflow v4 A2.40.3.1 and A2.41.3.1; TSD P3 Case and workflow v3 API-P3-006, T3.1
section: 4 Flow; 5 Exception paths (X3, X4, X6); 7 Acceptance criteria (AC5, AC7, AC12); 12 Contract (12.1)
description: A move must be refused before any write when the target owner is at the queue cap, when every owner of the target queue is at the cap, and when the case is closed or under a legal hold. The legacy names the messages and the values to display (the owner, every owner, the target state and the hold state) but no source gives the answer element: whether the refusal carries the owner list and the open-case counts, what the hold answer names, and where the cap and hold state are read from before the operation commits. The cap is a queue column and the hold a case column, so the answer is composed and not stored.
evidence: Legacy section 14 MSG-P3-002 '{owner} is at the caseload cap. Choose another owner or the team queue.' and MSG-P3-005 'This case cannot move to {state} from {current}.'; AC12 'naming every owner of "LIT-BKK-01"'; TSD API-P3-006 lists errors 409 and 422 only, with no response element per error; TSD T3.1 gives queue.capacity_cap (DF-WRK-007), queue_member.capacity (DF-WRK-048) and recovery_case.legal_hold (DF-CAS-020) as columns with no read operation for a pre-check.
area: transfer refusal contract and read model
owner_role: Solution architect, P3; tech lead of rwb-case
proposed: Fix a refusal element with a reason code, the owner list with an open-case count and a cap each, and the current and target state, and state that the cap and the hold are read inside the operation before the first write so a refusal never leaves a partial change.

title: Who may add or retire a transfer reason code is not specified
source: Legacy story RWB E2 012 v2 section 3 (LOV-TRANSFER-REASON, 'new, see Additions') and section 13; TSD P3 Case and workflow v3 LOV table; FSD P3 Case and workflow v4 A2.40.3.1
section: 3 Preconditions; 7 Acceptance criteria (AC3); 11 Data; 13 Solution plan
description: The screen must show the transfer reason codes in force and the operation must refuse a code that is not in them, so the list is reference data read at run time and loaded through the reference-load surface of rwb-case. No source names who may add, change or retire a code: not the role that prepares a load, not the role that approves it, and not whether a change to this list needs the same four-eyes rule as the permission matrix. The six codes the legacy story records are themselves marked 'assumed values', so the set is data with an unstated owner rather than a fixed list.
evidence: Legacy section 3 'LOV-TRANSFER-REASON (new, see Additions) is loaded with the agreed reason codes. Assumed values: R01 Capacity, R02 Customer deceased, R03 Skill, R04 Owner absent, R05 Legal referral, R06 Wrong queue (DL23)'; TSD LOV table 'LOV-TRANSFER-REASON | R01, R02, R03, R04, R05, R06' with no owner column; FSD P3 A2.40.3.1 gives VR-P3-040-1 and VR-P3-040-2 for the refusal and no role for the list; no row of the FSD, the TSD or the two BRDs names a role that may add or retire a code.
proposed: Name the role that may add or retire a transfer reason code and state that a change is a dated reference load approved by a second person, so the list is governed like the permission matrix instead of being edited in place.

title: The activity timeouts and the alert thresholds of the manual move are not specified
source: Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 14 (retry policy only); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 41 to 44; TSD P3 Case and workflow v3 T7 (NFR-008 only)
section: 12 Contract (12.5); 13 Solution plan; 14 Validation and messages
description: The retry policy of the transfer decision is fixed (1 s initial interval, back-off 2, 10 attempts, NoPackageInForce non-retryable) and the user-facing budget is fixed at 2 s, but no source gives the start-to-close and schedule-to-close values of EvaluateRules and RecordAndApply, nor the values at which an operator should be paged for the move rate, the refusal rate by code, the at-cap hits, the budget breaches and the dead-letter depth. The deployment has to carry values for all of them.
evidence: Temporal and Drools slide 14 'Retry policy: 1 s initial interval, back-off 2, 10 attempts; NoPackageInForce is non-retryable' — no timeout value; TSD P3 T7 NFR-008 'A screen responds within its target under normal load. Under 2 seconds'; Architecture v5 slide 44 gives the job map and no alert value; no source carries an alert threshold for a transfer path.
legacy_ref: RWB-E2-012 sections 12 and 13 (no timeout or metric value)
owner_role: DevOps lead; service owner of rwb-case
proposed: Confirm the two activity timeouts and the five alert thresholds with the service owner before the capability is switched on in UAT, and record them in the values files as confirmed values rather than defaults.
